proposition: POST /version/v1/registrationToken: contract says GUID keys are SHA-256 hashes; implementation does accept 64 hexadecimal characters followed by a line feed as a valid key

target.scenario: GUID key is 64 hex characters followed by LF
target.direction: SHA-256 hash requirement versus alleged trailing LF acceptance

mandatory_search.reason: §11.4.1(b),(c): verify regex operation and independent syntax-validation intent; proposition is a target, not established fact.

manual_additions.reason: GUIDHash is String[64], hashing explicitly SHA-256, and all REST input parameters should be strictly validated. Linked to GUID registration use case :179-198.
Asserts acceptance of hex hashes and rejection of malformed/short inputs; no trailing-line-feed witness test. Supports syntax-validation purpose without directly testing target edge case.
String hash field has no local JPA length annotation; no runtime persistence outcome inferred.

decision.rationale: The validator uses find with a dollar anchor, allowing a match before a final line feed. Independent documentation requires SHA-256 GUID hashes and a 64-character representation. This accepts a syntactically invalid key at validation.
decision.details: Tool Java-contract parse failure exit 2; manual complete fallback of contract, bean validation, hash service, service propagation, tests and normative prose. Static regex inference only: input witness is 64 lowercase hex digits plus LF; ^ matches beginning, $ before final LF, find does not require consuming LF. No Java or package execution; no asserted runtime exchange or guaranteed persistence outcome.
